questions.prompt: In K-means clustering, which of the following best describes the role of the initial centroids?

options.text: They are the final cluster centers.
They influence the final cluster configuration.
They determine the number of clusters.

questions.explanation: The starting centroids can lead to different local minima, affecting the final cluster assignment.

questions.prompt: In DBSCAN, what does the epsilon parameter primarily control?
questions.explanation: Epsilon sets the radius within which points are considered neighbors of a core point.

questions.prompt: Which linkage criterion in hierarchical clustering uses the smallest distance between any pair of points in two clusters?
questions.explanation: Single linkage defines the distance between clusters as the minimum distance between any two points in the clusters.

questions.prompt: K-means aims to minimize which of the following?

options.text: Sum of squared Euclidean distances within clusters.
Sum of Manhattan distances between cluster centers.
Sum of squared distances between points and nearest cluster center.
Sum of squared distances between cluster centers.

questions.explanation: The objective is to minimize the within-cluster sum of squared errors.

questions.prompt: In DBSCAN, points that are neither core nor border points are called?
questions.explanation: Such points are considered noise and are not assigned to any cluster.

questions.prompt: What is the time complexity of building a dendrogram using agglomerative hierarchical clustering with a naive implementation?
questions.explanation: Naively recomputing all pairwise distances at each merge step yields O(n^3) time.
